newsitem.title: USA: Shiva sees Q1 operating loss, charges.
newsitem.headline: Shiva sees Q1 operating loss, charges.

text.p: Shiva Corp said it will not meet analysts' expectations for revenues or earnings in its first quarter ended March 29 -- the second consecutive quarter in which Shiva has issued such a warning.
The company said it expected to take several non-recurring charges and to incur a substantial operating loss in the first quarter of 1997. It did not provide specific figures.

Shiva was expected to earn $0.07 per share in the quarter according to First Call. Shiva's stock plunged in early January after it warned that fourth quarter earnings were likely to be no more than a third of Wall Street expectations.
In pre-open trading Monday, Shiva was trading at 7-3/4, a record low, down more than a third from Thursday's close of 11-7/8.

Shiva said it is planning to take various financial actions in response to the shortfall, including substantial internal inventory writedowns, price cuts on some products, and additional promotional activities in the second quarter.

The company said that without these actions, first quarter revenue would likely have declined 15 to 25 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996. In the fourth quarter the company reported revenues of $48.2 million.
The company gave several causes for the shortfall.
It said sales to end users of its LanRover remote access products declined in the first quarter compared to the fourth quarter, largely as a result of increased price competition.
Shiva said estimated sales for the LanRover Access Switch concentrator also declined in the latest quarter due partly to delays in recognizing revenue at several large scale customer installations.
The network equipment maker also cited customer confusion surrounding the new higher-speed 56 kilobit modem technology as a factor.
Behind the confusion is a battle over a common industry standard for the higher speed Internet access technology.

Equipment makers have divided in two camps with one led by U.S. Robotics Corp, the first to ship the new modems and the other led by Rockwell International Corp and Lucent Technologies Inc, which includes Shiva.

It said the planned inventory writedowns in the first quarter were tied particulary to its v.34 modem cards, the existing generation of modem technology, in an apparent move to make way for the newer generation of 56 kilobit modems.
In addition, Shiva said it had shipped fewer products into selected sales channels to meet its previously stated goal to cut down on sales inventory backlog.
First quarter results will be reported in the company's regularly scheduled earnings announcement on April 17.
In a separate statement, Shiva said it had reached a three-year, mutually exclusive pact with Northern Telecom Ltd that provides Shiva with full Nortel funding for Shiva's Service Provider Group.
Shiva said it will receive from Nortel minimum quarterly royalty payments throughout 1997, and payments for manufacturing rights, support and research and development.
